mainTopic: רבי שמעון's rulings on mixed רקב, the שליא and the חררת דם (סופו כתחלתו and בטול ברוב), and the law of a corpse or fetus that lost its shape
overview: The amud opens by finishing off a rejected explanation of רבי שמעון's view that רקב (a corpse's dust) mixed with dirt is טהור. רבה gives a new reason, סופו כתחלתו: just as foreign material buried with a corpse cancels its רקב, so too foreign dirt mixed in later cancels it. The גמרא proves the first half from a ברייתא about corpses buried naked on stone versus in clothes, wood or on bricks. It then explains why the ברייתא needed both the case of mixed רקב and the case of scattered רקב. It also brings the case of cemetery dirt, which the רבנן call טמא because it surely holds a full תרווד of רקב. Next the גמרא asks why רבי שמעון rules a house with a miscarried שליא טהור. רבי יוחנן answers בטול ברוב, and he uses the same idea to explain רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling about an animal that expelled a חררת דם. רבי יוחנן adds that רבי שמעון agrees the mother is טמאה לידה, and an elder brings the source from 'אשה כי תזריע'. Finally, ריש לקיש compares a crushed fetus to a מת שנתבלבלה צורתו. רבי יוחנן asks how we know such a corpse is טהור, and the proposed source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One grain of dirt would just add to the amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes pushing away an earlier explanation of רבי שמעון: a single grain of dirt mixed in would simply count toward the amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a single grain of dirt got mixed in, it would just be absorbed and the required amount would be reached!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of an argument. The גמרא is knocking down an earlier explanation of רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny bit of outside dirt should simply get swallowed up in the corpse's dust and add to its measure. So the earlier reasoning cannot be why רבי שמעון rules as he does. This clears the way for a new explanation.

phrases.english: One grain of dirt,
and the measure would be filled by it!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּרִידָה אַחַת עָפָר, וְנָפֵיל לֵיהּ שִׁיעוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a rejection begun on the earlier part of the daf
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier explanation of רבי שמעון's reasoning
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A small amount of outside dirt would be absorbed and count toward the measure. It would not undo the טומאה.

steps.title: רבה: the corpse's end stage follows its beginning stage
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains רבי שמעון with the rule סופו כתחלתו: at both stages, a foreign substance mixed in cancels the טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: This is רבי שמעון's reason. The end is like the beginning. At the beginning, something else mixed in cancels it. So too at the end, something else mixed in cancels it.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first explanation fell, רבה offers a new reason for רבי שמעון. The corpse in its final dust state follows the same rule as in its earlier state.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a known rule: when a corpse decays, dust from another material mixed in cancels the טומאה of רקב. רבה says the same 'cancelling' applies later on. So even a small foreign mixture undoes the special טומאה, and it is not simply absorbed. The new idea is that mixing does not just add to the measure; it ruins the category.

keyTerms.meaning: Its end is like its beginning: the same rule applies at both stages
Something that cancels or nullifies the טומאה

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes how we view mixtures in רקב. A foreign substance is not treated as harmless. It cancels the טומאה entirely.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Shimon:
its end is like its beginning —
just as at its beginning, there becomes for it
another substance as a cancellation,
phrases.notes: Something foreign mixed into the decaying corpse cancels the טומאה of its dust.

phrases.english: so too at its end, there becomes for it
another substance as a cancellation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A little foreign dirt would just be absorbed into the corpse's dust.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like at the earlier stage, any foreign substance cancels the טומאה of the corpse's dust.

steps.title: Where is the rule about the beginning stage taught?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source teaches that a foreign substance cancels the טומאה of the corpse's dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants to see the source for the 'beginning stage' rule רבה relied on, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה built his argument on a known rule. Before accepting the comparison, the גמרא identifies where that rule is stated.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for the source being referred to)

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He means: what source teaches the 'beginning stage' rule רבה just used?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבה's comparison
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that foreign material mixed with a decaying corpse cancels its רקב.

steps.title: A corpse buried with nothing else around it has רקב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that a body buried naked in a marble coffin or on a stone floor has רקב that is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: Which corpse has רקב, and which corpse does not have רקב? If he was buried naked in a marble coffin or on a stone floor, that corpse has רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The first case is when the corpse's dust does count as טמא רקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marble and stone do not crumble into dust, and the body has no clothes. So any dust found there must come only from the corpse. That pure, unmixed corpse-dust is רקב and is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The decayed dust of a corpse, which can be טמא

steps.confusionAlert: 'Has רקב' does not mean the body decays more. It means its dust has the halachic status of רקב, so it is טמא.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Which is a corpse that has רקב,
and which is a corpse that does not have רקב?
If he was buried naked in a marble coffin

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי רִצְפָּה שֶׁל אֲבָנִים —
phrases.english: or on a stone floor —
that is a corpse that has רקב.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵיזֶהוּ מֵת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רָקָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only unmixed corpse-dust is רקב

steps.title: A corpse buried with clothes, wood or bricks has no רקב
steps.stepSummary: If the body was buried in its clothes, in a wooden coffin, or on a brick floor, its dust is not טמא as רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which corpse does not have רקב? If he was buried in his clothes, or in a wooden coffin, or on a brick floor, that corpse does not have רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opposite case. Here the dust does not count as רקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothes, wood and bricks all crumble into dust over time. That dust mixes with the corpse's dust. Because something foreign is mixed in, the dust loses its status as רקב. This is exactly the 'beginning stage' rule רבה used.
steps.whatToRemember: Only dust that comes entirely from the corpse counts as רקב. Any outside material mixed in cancels it. רבה says this is true at the end stage too.

phrases.english: And which is a corpse that does not have רקב?
If he was buried in his clothing,
or in a wooden coffin,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי רִצְפָּה שֶׁל לְבֵנִים —
phrases.english: or on a brick floor —
that is a corpse that does not have רקב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזֶהוּ מֵת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ רָקָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, giving the opposite case
steps.raayaObject: רבה's 'beginning stage' rule that foreign material cancels רקב

steps.title: רקב applies only to someone who died naturally
steps.stepSummary: The rule of רקב is limited to a person who died a natural death. It does not apply to someone who was killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they said רקב only for a corpse alone, which excludes one who was killed, who does not have it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more limit on the law of רקב. It applies only to a person who died naturally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'corpse' (מת) here is read narrowly. Someone who was killed is excluded, so his dust does not carry the טומאה of רקב. This is a separate limit, beyond the rule about mixtures.

phrases.english: And they did not say רקב
except for a corpse alone,
phrases.notes: Here 'corpse' means someone who died a natural death.

phrases.english: to exclude one who was killed, who does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ רָקָב אֶלָּא לְמֵת בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit to the ברייתא's law of רקב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טומאה of רקב applies only to one who died naturally, not to one who was killed.

steps.title: Returning to the ברייתא: mixed רקב and scattered רקב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives two cases. In the first, dirt fell into a תרווד of רקב. In the second, a תרווד of רקב was scattered around a house. In both, the רבנן say טמא and רבי שמעון says טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the ברייתא itself: if any amount of dirt fell into a full ladle of רקב, it is טמא, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור. If a full ladle of רקב was scattered around a house, the house is טמא, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes, in full, the ברייתא it mentioned earlier about רבי שמעון's view. This sets up the next move: explaining why the ברייתא needed both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate cases. In the first, the רקב is all in one place but mixed with ordinary dirt. In the second, the רקב is pure corpse-dust but spread out across the house. In both cases the רבנן keep the טומאה and רבי שמעון cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא is going back to look closely at a source it quoted before.
A full ladle of corpse-dust, the smallest amount that brings טומאת אהל.
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit.

phrases.english: The matter itself: a full ladle of corpse-dust
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא about רבי שמעון quoted earlier on the daf, the one רבה explained in Step 2.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכוֹ עָפָר כֹּל שֶׁהוּא — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: into which any amount of dirt fell is impure,
and Rabbi Shimon declares it pure.
A full ladle of corpse-dust that was scattered in the house:
the house is impure, and Rabbi Shimon declares it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the source for בטול by a foreign substance, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא behind רבי שמעון's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed רקב and scattered רקב: the רבנן say טמא and רבי שמעון says טהור.

steps.title: Why the scattered case is needed
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא had taught only the mixed case, we might have thought the רבנן say טמא only because the רקב is all together. With scattered רקב, they might have agreed with רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both cases are needed. If we had only the first one, I would say the רבנן call it טמא there because the dust is gathered in one place. But when it is scattered, maybe they agree with רבי שמעון that covering one small pile and then another small pile does not add up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא had to teach both cases. This step shows what we would have mistakenly thought if we had only the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the mixed case, all the רקב is still in one spot, so it is easy to say it brings טומאה. In the scattered case, the roof covers only small bits here and there. There is a rule that covering one too-small amount and then another too-small amount does not combine, so we might have thought even the רבנן would say טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is needed.' This is the opening of a צְרִיכוּתָא, which explains why both cases had to be taught.
Covering one small amount and then covering another small amount does not combine them into a full amount for טומאת אהל.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'אין מאהיל וחוזר ומאהיל' does not mean the scattered רקב stops being רקב. It only means that separate small piles under one roof might not join together to reach a full תרווד.

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if it had taught us only the first case,
in that case the Rabbis say it is impure
because it is gathered together,
but if it was scattered,
I might say they agree with Rabbi Shimon,
that covering one small amount and then covering another does not combine.
phrases.notes: He means the roof covers one little pile here and another little pile there, and those don't add up to a full ladle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא in Step 7 needed its second case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the mixed case, we might think the רבנן would agree with רבי שמעון when the רקב is scattered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The scattered case teaches that the רבנן say טמא even when the רקב is spread out.

steps.title: Why the mixed case is needed
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא had taught only the scattered case, we might have thought רבי שמעון says טהור only there, because of אין מאהיל וחוזר ומאהיל. In the mixed case, he might have agreed with the רבנן. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only the scattered case, I would say רבי שמעון calls it טהור only there, because covering bit after bit does not combine. But in the mixed case, maybe he agrees with the רבנן. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא from the other direction and concludes that both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's reason in the scattered case could have been only that separate piles don't combine. That reason does not work in the mixed case, where the רקב is all together. So the mixed case teaches that, for רבי שמעון, a foreign substance mixed in cancels the טומאה on its own, the rule from Step 2.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side's view needed a separate case. The scattered case shows the רבנן's view is strong, so they say טמא even when the רקב is spread out. The mixed case shows רבי שמעון's view is strong, so he says טהור even when the רקב is all together.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' here means the scattered one.

phrases.english: in this case Rabbi Shimon says it is pure
because covering one small amount and then another does not combine,
but in that case,
phrases.notes: Now 'that case' switches back to the first one, where dirt fell into the רקב.

phrases.english: I might say he agrees with the Rabbis;
therefore it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא started in Step 8 from the other direction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the scattered case, we might think רבי שמעון would agree that mixed רקב is טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are needed, so neither one is extra.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: a little more than a ladle of cemetery dirt
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that a little more than a תרווד of dirt from a בית הקברות is טמא, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: a full ladle and a little more of cemetery dirt is טמא, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא where the same two sides argue, this time about dirt taken from a cemetery. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we don't know for sure that there is any רקב in the dirt at all. Even so, the רבנן say it is טמא, which needs an explanation. רבי שמעון's view fits his idea that dirt mixed in cancels the טומאה.

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: מְלֹא תַּרְוָד וְעוֹד עֲפַר בֵּית הַקְּבָרוֹת — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: a full ladle and a bit more of cemetery dirt is impure,
and Rabbi Shimon declares it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related argument between the same sides, now about cemetery dirt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A little more than a תרווד of cemetery dirt: the רבנן say טמא, and רבי שמעון says טהור.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן say the cemetery dirt is טמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for the רבנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן say plain cemetery dirt is טמא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cemetery dirt is mostly ordinary earth, and we are not sure it holds any corpse-dust. So the גמרא wants to know why the רבנן treat it as definitely bringing טומאה.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the רבנן's ruling in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a little more than a תרווד of cemetery dirt is treated as טמא.

steps.title: There must be a ladle of רקב inside
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reason that a little more than a תרווד of cemetery dirt must contain a full תרווד of רקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is impossible for a full ladle and a bit more of cemetery dirt not to have a full ladle of corpse-dust in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן assume such dirt surely has a full תרווד of רקב inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן assume that cemetery dirt of a little more than a תרווד will surely hold a full תרווד of רקב somewhere in it. The ordinary earth mixed in does not cancel the טומאה for them, just like in Step 7. רבי שמעון disagrees because, for him, mixed-in dirt cancels it.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן assume that a little more than a תרווד of cemetery dirt must hold a full תרווד of רקב, so it is טמא. רבי שמעון stays with his view that a foreign substance mixed in cancels the טומאה.

phrases.english: Because it is impossible

phrases.aramaic: לִמְלֹא תַּרְוָד וְעוֹד עֲפַר בֵּית הַקְּבָרוֹת
phrases.english: for a full ladle and a bit more of cemetery dirt
not to contain a full ladle of corpse-dust.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A little more than a תרווד of cemetery dirt surely contains a full תרווד of רקב, so it is טמא.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason for the שליא case?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון's reason for mixed רקב is סופו כתחלתו, the גמרא asks what his reason is for ruling the house טהור in the case of a שליא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you say רבי שמעון's reason is that a body's final state follows the same rule as its first state, what is his reason in the case of a שליא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the reason it just found for רבי שמעון does not fit his other ruling about a שליא. So it asks for a new reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון's ruling seemed to come from a different idea. Now we know his reason in the dirt case is סופו כתחלתו. That idea says nothing about a miscarried שליא, so his ruling there still needs its own explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Afterbirth. A house with a miscarried שליא is normally treated as טמא, because there is no שליא without a ולד.

phrases.english: Now that you say
the reason of Rabbi Shimon
is because its end is like its beginning,
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's reason in the case of a corpse's dust that has dirt mixed into it.

phrases.english: regarding an afterbirth, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: In that case רבי שמעון also rules the house is טהור, and the גמרא wants to know why.

steps.triggerLanguage: השתא דאמרת טעמא דרבי שמעון משום סופו כתחלתו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The explanation of רבי שמעון from the earlier steps leaves his שליא ruling unexplained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי שמעון rules a house טהור when a שליא was miscarried in it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ולד is nullified by the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the dissolved ולד is nullified by the larger amount of blood that came out with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: they ruled this way because of nullification in a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives רבי שמעון's reason. Whatever is left of the ולד is lost in the much larger amount of blood, so it does not make the house טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is בטול ברוב. A small thing mixed into a larger amount of something else loses its own status. The leftover of the ולד is a small amount inside a majority of blood, so its טומאה is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullification in a majority. A small amount mixed into a larger amount loses its own status.
Literally, they touched it. Here it means the חכמים based their ruling on this idea.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
because of nullification in a majority
they touched upon it.
phrases.notes: He means the ruling of טהור is based on this reason. The ולד is lost in the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן משום בטול ברוב נגעו בה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dissolved ולד is nullified by the majority of blood, so the house is טהור.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: two תנאים said the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, since he said רבי שמעון and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב hold the same idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, for רבי יוחנן said: רבי שמעון and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's answer matches something else he said. This sets up the next steps, which show the two rulings he is comparing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן links two different תנאים to one idea. The next steps show that the shared idea is בטול ברוב.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning. He is consistent with what he says elsewhere.
One thing. Both rulings are based on the same idea.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
said one thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואזדא רבי יוחנן לטעמיה דאמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14 by showing that רבי יוחנן uses this idea elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב both rule based on the same principle.

steps.title: The two rulings: the שליא and the חררת דם
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's ruling is the שליא case. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rules that a large animal that expelled a mass of blood must bury it and is פטורה מן הבכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון's ruling is the one we just said. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling is taught in a ברייתא: a large animal that expelled a mass of congealed blood must have it buried, and the animal is exempt from the law of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the two rulings רבי יוחנן was comparing. The second one is about an animal that gave birth to a lump of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By being פטורה מן הבכורה, the mother is treated as having already given birth. Her next calf is not a בכור, which means the lump is treated as having a real ולד. Why the lump must be buried is asked and answered in Steps 18–19.

keyTerms.meaning: A large domestic animal, such as a cow.
Exempt from the בכור law. Her next offspring will not count as a firstborn.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon: that which we said,
phrases.notes: This is the שליא case from steps 13–14.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer: as it is taught:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
A large animal that expelled a mass of blood,
this must be buried,
and it is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי שמעון הא דאמרן רבי אליעזר דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the two rulings mentioned in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חררת דם from a large animal must be buried, and the mother is פטורה מן הבכורה.

steps.title: רבי חייא: the mass gives no טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא adds that the חררת דם does not make things טמא by touching or by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא taught about it: it does not make things impure, neither by touching nor by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא adds a detail to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling. The lump does not carry the טומאה of a dead animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead fetus would normally be a נבלה, which is מטמא by מגע and by משא. רבי חייא says this lump is not. This creates a tension that the גמרא will now explore.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching. One way טומאה is passed on.
Carrying. Another way טומאה is passed on, even without touching.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya taught about it:
it does not make impure
neither by touching nor by carrying,

steps.triggerLanguage: ותני רבי חייא עלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling to the ברייתא of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חררת דם is not מטמא by מגע or by משא.

steps.title: If it gives no טומאה, why bury it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the lump is not מטמא at all, why does it need burial?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it does not make things impure by touching or by carrying, why must it be buried?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the burial rule. A lump that gives no טומאה seems not to be a real ולד, so burying it looks pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial suggests the lump might be a holy בכור. Not being מטמא suggests it is not a ולד at all. The two rulings seem to pull in opposite directions.

phrases.english: And since it does not make impure
neither by touching nor by carrying,
why must it be buried?

steps.triggerLanguage: ומאחר שאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא אמאי תקבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 16 and step 17 fit together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The burial rule of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, set against רבי חייא's ruling that the lump is not מטמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not being מטמא implies the lump is not a ולד, so there should be no reason to bury it.

steps.title: Burial lets people know the mother is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The lump is buried to make it public that the mother is פטורה מן הבכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To publicize that she is exempt from the firstborn law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the burial is not about holiness or טומאה. It lets everyone know that this animal's next calf is not a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burial is a public signal. It prevents people from mistakenly treating the next calf as a holy בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: To publicize it, to make it known.

phrases.english: In order to publicize it
that it is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: כדי לפרסמה שהיא פטורה מן הבכורה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different purpose for the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burial must mean the lump is a holy or טמא ולד.
steps.terutzMaskana: Burial is only a public sign that the mother is פטורה מן הבכורה.

steps.title: If it counts as a real ולד, why no טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses: being פטורה מן הבכורה shows the lump is a real ולד, so why does רבי חייא say it is not מטמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: So it is a real offspring. Then why does רבי חייא teach that it does not make things impure by touching or by carrying?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer just given creates a new problem. If the lump counts as a birth, it is a real ולד, and a dead ולד should be מטמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exempting the mother from בכורה only makes sense if the lump is a full ולד. A full dead ולד should carry the טומאה of נבלה. So רבי חייא's ruling seems to contradict this.

phrases.english: Evidently it is a full offspring,
so why does Rabbi Chiyya teach:
it does not make impure
neither by touching nor by carrying?

steps.triggerLanguage: אלמא ולד מעליא הוא ואמאי תני רבי חייא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 19's answer to raise a new contradiction with step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling that the lump is not מטמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lump counts as a real birth for בכורה, it is a real ולד and should be מטמא like a נבלה.

steps.title: Again בטול ברוב: the ולד is lost in the blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the ולד is real, but it is nullified by the majority of blood, so it gives no טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: they ruled this way because of nullification in a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן resolves the contradiction with the same idea he used for רבי שמעון's שליא case. This shows why he said both תנאים said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בכורה, the lump counts as a real birth. For טומאה, the small ולד is nullified inside the larger mass of blood, so it is not מטמא. This matches step 14, where the dissolved ולד is lost in the blood and the house is טהור.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן explains both רבי שמעון (the שליא) and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (the חררת דם) with one idea, בטול ברוב. A real ולד mixed into a majority of blood loses its טומאה.
steps.confusionAlert: בטול ברוב does not erase the birth itself. The mother is still פטורה מן הבכורה. Only the טומאה of the ולד is cancelled.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
because of nullification in a majority
they touched upon it.
phrases.notes: Same words as step 14. Here the ולד is lost inside the rest of the blood lump.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן משום בטול ברוב נגעו בה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 and completes the parallel claimed in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two laws: the lump counts as a birth for בכורה, but it is nullified for טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A real ולד must be מטמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ולד is nullified in the majority of blood, so it is not מטמא, even though the mother is פטורה מן הבכורה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב both rely on בטול ברוב, just as רבי יוחנן said.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees the mother is impure from childbirth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי quotes רבי יוחנן: even ר' שמעון, who says the house is טהור, agrees that the mother is טמאה לידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי שמעון agrees that the mother is impure with the impurity of childbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to ר' שמעון's opinion about a שליא. רבי יוחנן adds that ר' שמעון still agrees the woman herself is טמאה לידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ר' שמעון said the שליא does not make the house טמא. One might think this means he treats it as if no birth happened at all. רבי יוחנן says no: the mother still has טומאת לידה, even though the house stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees (on this point, even though he argues on other points)
impure with the impurity of a woman who gave birth
its mother (the woman who passed it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of טומאה here. The house can stay טהור while the mother is still טמאה לידה. They are separate questions.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
And Rabbi Shimon agrees
that its mother is impure from childbirth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁאִמּוֹ טְמֵאָה לֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חררת דם discussion and returns to ר' שמעון's view on a שליא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to ר' שמעון, a woman who passes a שליא is טמאה לידה.

steps.title: An elder explains רבי יוחנן's reason from a verse
steps.stepSummary: An elder tells רבי אמי that the reason comes from the פסוק 'אשה כי תזריע': even if what she births looks only like seed, she is טמאה לידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to רבי אמי: I will explain רבי יוחנן's reason to you. The verse says, 'A woman who bears seed and gives birth to a male.' This teaches that even if she gives birth to something that looks only like the seed she bore, she is impure from childbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: An elder gives a פסוק that supports רבי יוחנן's statement from step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word תזריע, which means 'bears seed.' The elder reads this as teaching that even a birth that looks like plain seed, with no clear shape, still counts as a לידה for the mother. So the mother can be טמאה לידה even when the thing she passed does not look like a formed baby.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to Rabbi Ami:
I will explain to you Rabbi Yochanan's reason,
for the verse says:
"If a woman bears seed and gives birth to a male, etc."
even if she gave birth to nothing
except something like the seed she bore,
phrases.notes: He means something that has melted down and looks like seed, with no baby's shape.

phrases.english: she is impure from childbirth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for רבי יוחנן's statement in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that ר' שמעון agrees the mother is טמאה לידה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word תזריע in ויקרא 12:2, which teaches that even a seed-like birth makes the mother טמאה לידה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a crushed fetus is like a corpse that lost its shape
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says a שפיר that was crushed in its own fluids is treated like a מת שנתבלבלה צורתו, a corpse whose shape was ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: a fetus in its sac that was crushed in its fluids becomes like a corpse whose shape has been ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a new rule about a שפיר whose contents were mashed. He compares it to a מת that lost its human shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שפיר is the sac that holds a fetus. If it was shaken until the fetus was mashed in the fluid, the fetus no longer has a form. ריש לקיש says it gets the same law as a מת whose shape is ruined, which he assumes is טהור. In the next step רבי יוחנן asks for the source of that assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: its shape became ruined or unrecognizable

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A fetal sac that was crushed in its fluids
becomes like a corpse
whose shape was ruined.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: שָׁפִיר שֶׁטְּרָפוּהוּ בְּמֵימָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion, still about births that have no clear form.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crushed שפיר has the law of a מת שנתבלבלה צורתו.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks for the source that a ruined corpse is pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks ריש לקיש how we know that a מת שנתבלבלה צורתו is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: A corpse whose shape was ruined, how do we know it is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן questions the base of ריש לקיש's comparison. Where do we learn that a ruined corpse is טהור at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule only works if a ruined מת is טהור. רבי יוחנן asks for the source of that idea. If there is no good source, the comparison falls apart.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to Reish Lakish:
A corpse whose shape was ruined,
from where do we know that it is pure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת שֶׁנִּתְבַּלְבְּלָה צוּרָתוֹ מְנָלַן דְּטָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption that ריש לקיש's comparison in step 24 depends on.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's assumption that a מת שנתבלבלה צורתו is טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison only holds if the ruined מת is טהור, so a source for that is needed.

steps.title: A proposed source: a burned corpse with its skeleton intact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a source: רבי שבתאי and רבי יצחק מגדלאה taught that a burned מת whose skeleton is still whole is טמא, and there was a case where they declared the large doorways טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learn it from what רבי שבתאי said in the name of רבי יצחק מגדלאה (and some say רבי יצחק מגדלאה said it in the name of רבי שבתאי): a corpse that was burned but its skeleton is still whole is impure. There was such a case, and they declared the large doorways impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to suggest where the rule might come from, using a teaching about a burned מת. This sets up the next move, which will check whether this source really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching says a burned מת is טמא when its skeleton is still whole. That seems to suggest that if the shape is gone, it would be טהור. This is the proposed source for ריש לקיש's assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (opens a suggestion that may be rejected)
its skeleton or frame, its overall shape

phrases.english: If you say it is from this,
which Rabbi Shabbtai said
that Rabbi Yitzchak of Migdal said,
and some say it
as Rabbi Yitzchak of Migdal said
that Rabbi Shabbtai said:
A corpse that was burned
but its skeleton is still whole is impure.
There was such a case,
and they declared the large doorways impure because of it.
phrases.notes: These are doorways the body could be carried out through, so whatever was under them became טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שַׁבְּתַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to רבי יוחנן's question in step 25, using an אילימא, which is a suggestion the גמרא may go on to reject.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a מת שנתבלבלה צורתו is טהור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי שבתאי and רבי יצחק מגדלאה that a burned מת is טמא only when its skeleton is whole, along with the case of the large doorways.
